# Flint ingest queue

The order in which sources go into the vault library. Each course or book is atomized
by Sonnet into `staging/library/` and reviewed by Codex against its source, following
the ingest review gate. Only then is it copied into SecondBrain, indexed and committed.

## Promoted to the vault

- **Harries, The Fundamentals of On-Field Rehabilitation**: 33 entries, domain `rehab-and-return-to-play`. SecondBrain `c15460d` (2026-09-26), after two review rounds by an independent Opus reviewer (Codex was capped) and nine reciprocal links. Harries batch 2 is pending: 5 items the first pass missed (the case-review template, fitting rehab into the team week, the HSR format progression, the mid-rehab hamstring checkpoint, and speed prescription in late rehab).
- **2026-09-27, SecondBrain `aacbccd`:** Harries batch 2 (+4, now 37); Old Bull course (37, new domain `performance-technology-and-leadership`); Issurin *Block Periodization* Ch1-3 (28); Bondarchuk *Transfer of Training* I Ch1-2 (20); *Supertraining* Ch1-3 (113); Landon Evans *Elite Sports Performance* lectures (34). Every source went through independent Opus falsification reviews, with a round 2 where fixes were heavy. Resume points: *Supertraining* Ch4, Issurin Ch4, Bondarchuk I Ch3.

## In progress

1. (promoted, see above) **Harries**.
   - Domain: new `rehab-and-return-to-play`. Book slug: `on-field-rtp--harries`.
   - Stance: Eric's 2026-09-25 review. Keep it as a dosage reference; the theory is Taberner's control-chaos continuum with a velocity layer.
2. **Old Bull Performance course**.
   - Domain: new `performance-technology-and-leadership`. Book slug: `old-bull-performance-course--old-bull`.

## Next: Landon Evans (queued 2026-09-26 by Eric)

681 unique files. Most of it is a curated library Landon gave Eric (`From Landon Evans/Eric Files/`), not Landon's own writing. Landon's own teaching goes first, because it is his voice that gets compared with Eric's method.

| Step | What | Files | Route |

# /// script
# requires-python = ">=3.10"
# ///
"""Step 2a: tag every unique manifest file with disciplines and a route, by rules only.

    uv run scripts/triage_rules.py

Reads data/manifest.csv, writes data/triage.csv (all unique files) and
data/unclassified.csv (the rules found no discipline; these go to the cheap-model
pass), plus data/triage_summary.md (aggregate counts, committed). No tokens spent.
Disciplines match the section names in docs/method-baseline.md.
"""
import csv
import re
from collections import Counter
from pathlib import Path

DATA = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / "data"

# Keyword rules, matched case-insensitively against "path/name". A file can carry
# several disciplines. Named coach and course folders are listed with the topic they
# are mostly about, so TB's subfolder names classify whole collections.
DISCIPLINES = {
    "Speed and sprint": r"sprint|speed(?!s? ?up)|accelerat|max(imal)?[ _-]?velocity|top[ _-]?speed|agility|\bcod\b|change[ _-]of[ _-]direction|decel|hurdl|track and field|charlie francis|altis|speedworks|huntington|shexnayder|moyer|natera|\bscn\b|ken clark|korfist",
    "Strength and power": r"strength|power|squat|deadlift|bench|olympic|weightlift|\bclean\b|snatch|\bjerk\b|triphasic|velocity[ _-]based|\bvbt\b|isometric|eccentric|plyometric|hypertroph|powerlift|conjugate|westside|kilo|poliquin|thibaudeau|wendler|juggernaut|travis mash|vermeil|flywheel|\bapre\b",
    "Conditioning and energy systems": r"condition|energy[ _-]system|aerobic|anaerobic|\bvo2|interval|lactate|heart[ _-]rate|endurance|repeat(ed)?[ _-]sprint|jamieson|metabolic",
    "Rehab and return to play": r"rehab|return[ _-]to[ _-](play|sport|run)|\brtp\b|\brts\b|\bacl\b|hamstring|tendin|tendon|achilles|ankle|rotator|scap|shoulder|knee|\bhip\b|groin|spine|back[ _-]pain|concussion|surgery|post[ _-]?op|physio|therap|stop chasing pain|david gr[ae]y|\bdns\b|burdenko|eldoa|\bpri\b|postural restoration|z-health|functional ?range|kinstretch|knees over toes|trigger point|soft tissue|\biaom\b|gray institute|tissue loading|aspetar|harries|crossover symmetry|cressey|\brpr\b",
    "Injury risk and prevention": r"injur|prevention|\bacwr\b|nordic|nordbord|screen|\bfms\b|risk",
    "Load monitoring and GPS": r"workload|training[ _-]load|\bload\b|\bgps\b|monitor|\brpe\b|wellness|\bhrv\b|fatigue|readiness|monotony|strain|acute|chronic",
    "Testing and assessment": r"force[ _-]?plate|\bcmj\b|countermovement|jump|testing|assessment|benchmark|profil|f-?v\b|force[ _-]velocity|\bvald\b|hawkin|isokinetic|\bimtp\b|\bdsi\b|\brsi\b|\bpca\b|combine|pro ?day",
    "Recovery and sleep": r"recover|sleep|regenerat|cold[ _-]water|cryo|sauna|massage|compression|vibration",
    "Nutrition and body composition": r"nutrition|diet|protein|carbohydr|hydrat|supplement|creatine|body[ _-]comp|dexa|fat[ _-]loss|weight[ _-](loss|gain)|precision nutrition|lyle mcdonald|energy availability|red-?s\b|ben house|renaissance periodization|caffeine",
    "Coaching, skill acquisition and constraints-led approach": r"skill|constraint|ecological|motor[ _-]learning|coaching|\bcue|attention|percept|dynamical|representative|bosch|myszka|rob gray|\bcla\b|conscious coach",
    "Periodization and programming": r"periodi|programm|annual[ _-]plan|\bblock\b|macrocycle|mesocycle|taper|verkhoshansk|bondarchuk|issurin|matveyev|bompa|zatsiorsk|siff|supertraining|planning|planner|template|yessis|windows of trainability",
    "Anatomy, physiology and biomechanics": r"anatom|physiolog|biomechan|anatomy trains|myers|kinesiolog|neuromuscular|muscle|fascia",
    "Data, technology and reporting": r"\bdata\b|analytic|statistic|python|\br\b programming|dashboard|machine[ _-]learning|excel|\breport|technology|smartabase|\bams\b|mladen|jovanovic|patrick ward",
    "Leadership, culture and psychology": r"leader|psycholog|mental|mindset|culture|communicat|management|motivat|old ?bull",
    "Female athlete": r"female|women|menstru|pregnan",
    "Youth and development": r"youth|\bltad\b|long[ _-]term[ _-]athlete|adolescen|maturation|\bphv\b",
}
RULES = {k: re.compile(v, re.I) for k, v in DISCIPLINES.items()}

# Named collections worth tracking as units. TB and Landon come from the manifest's
# collections column (it follows every duplicate copy); the rest match on path.
COLLECTIONS = {
    "Mike Golden library": r"Golden, Mike",
    "Old Bull Performance": r"old ?bull",
    "Harries On-Field RTP (Sportsmith)": r"SS.Course.OnFieldRTP",
    "CVASPS": r"cvasp",
    "ALTIS": r"altis",
    "Charlie Francis": r"charlie ?francis",
}
COLLECTION_RULES = {k: re.compile(v, re.I) for k, v in COLLECTIONS.items()}

# Eric's own generated reports and dashboards: a record of practice, not literature.
OWN_REPORTS = re.compile(r"DASHBOARDS_AND_REPORTS|Report_Templates", re.I)


def route(row: dict) -> str:
    if OWN_REPORTS.search(row["path"]):
        return "Eric's reports (archive)"
    if row.get("in_zotero") == "True":
        return "already in Zotero"
    kind, size = row["kind"], int(row["size"] or 0)
    if kind in ("video", "audio"):
        return "transcription queue"
    if kind == "paper_or_book":
        if row["ext"] in ("epub", "mobi") or size >= 8_000_000:
            return "book (ingest-book, gated)"
        return "paper (Zotero)"
    if kind in ("document", "slides"):
        return "vault atomize"
    if kind == "data":
        return "template or data (review)"
    return "catalog only"


def main() -> None:
    with open(DATA / "manifest.csv", encoding="utf-8-sig") as fh:
        rows = [r for r in csv.DictReader(fh) if r["canonical"] == "True"]
    out, unclassified = [], []
    for r in rows:
        # A Zotero title (recovered by md5) rescues files named only by a Drive ID.
        text = f"{r['source']}/{r['path']} {r.get('zotero_title', '')}".replace("_", " ")
        rt = route(r)
        # Reports keep no discipline tags so they do not inflate the literature counts.
        tags = [] if rt == "Eric's reports (archive)" else [k for k, rx in RULES.items() if rx.search(text)]
        colls = [c for c in (r.get("collections") or "").split(";") if c]
        colls += [k for k, rx in COLLECTION_RULES.items() if rx.search(text)]
        r = {**r, "disciplines": ";".join(tags), "route": rt, "collections": ";".join(sorted(set(colls)))}
        out.append(r)
        if not tags and rt != "Eric's reports (archive)":
            unclassified.append(r)
    fields = list(out[0])
    for name, subset in (("triage.csv", out), ("unclassified.csv", unclassified)):
        with open(DATA / name, "w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            w = csv.DictWriter(fh, fieldnames=fields)
            w.writeheader()
            w.writerows(subset)

    disc = Counter(t for r in out for t in r["disciplines"].split(";") if t)
    routes = Counter(r["route"] for r in out)
    reports = sum(r["route"] == "Eric's reports (archive)" for r in out)
    lit = len(out) - reports
    lines = [
        "# Flint triage summary (rules pass)", "",
        f"Unique files: {len(out)}, of which {reports} are Eric's own reports and dashboards (archived, not classified). "
        f"Of the other {lit}, the rules classified {lit - len(unclassified)} ({100 * (lit - len(unclassified)) / lit:.0f}%); "
        f"{len(unclassified)} are left for the model pass (`data/unclassified.csv`).",
        "A file can carry several disciplines, so discipline counts sum to more than the file count.", "",
        "## By discipline", "", "| Discipline | Files | Papers/books | Video/audio |", "|---|---:|---:|---:|",
    ]
    for k, n in disc.most_common():
        sub = [r for r in out if k in r["disciplines"].split(";")]
        pb = sum(r["kind"] == "paper_or_book" for r in sub)
        av = sum(r["kind"] in ("video", "audio") for r in sub)
        lines.append(f"| {k} | {n} | {pb} | {av} |")
    lines += ["", "## By route", "", "| Route | Files |", "|---|---:|"]
    lines += [f"| {k} | {n} |" for k, n in routes.most_common()]
    coll = Counter(c for r in out for c in r["collections"].split(";") if c)
    lines += ["", "## Named collections", "", "| Collection | Files | Papers/books | Video/audio |", "|---|---:|---:|---:|"]
    for k, n in coll.most_common():
        sub = [r for r in out if k in r["collections"].split(";")]
        pb = sum(r["kind"] == "paper_or_book" for r in sub)
        av = sum(r["kind"] in ("video", "audio") for r in sub)
        lines.append(f"| {k} | {n} | {pb} | {av} |")
    (DATA / "triage_summary.md").write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
    print("\n".join(lines))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

    "Rehab and return to play": r"rehab|return[ _-]to[ _-](play|sport|run)|\brtp\b|\brts\b|\bacl\b|hamstring|tendin|tendon|achilles|ankle|rotator|scap|shoulder|knee|\bhip\b|groin|spine|back[ _-]pain|concussion|surgery|post[ _-]?op|physio|therap|stop chasing pain|david gr[ae]y|\bdns\b|burdenko|eldoa|\bpri\b|postural restoration|z-health|functional ?range|kinstretch|knees over toes|trigger point|soft tissue|\biaom\b|gray institute|tissue loading|aspetar|harries|crossover symmetry|cressey|\brpr\b",
    "Injury risk and prevention": r"injur|prevention|\bacwr\b|nordic|nordbord|screen|\bfms\b|risk",
    "Load monitoring and GPS": r"workload|training[ _-]load|\bload\b|\bgps\b|monitor|\brpe\b|wellness|\bhrv\b|fatigue|readiness|monotony|strain|acute|chronic",
    "Testing and assessment": r"force[ _-]?plate|\bcmj\b|countermovement|jump|testing|assessment|benchmark|profil|f-?v\b|force[ _-]velocity|\bvald\b|hawkin|isokinetic|\bimtp\b|\bdsi\b|\brsi\b|\bpca\b|combine|pro ?day",
    "Recovery and sleep": r"recover|sleep|regenerat|cold[ _-]water|cryo|sauna|massage|compression|vibration",
    "Nutrition and body composition": r"nutrition|diet|protein|carbohydr|hydrat|supplement|creatine|body[ _-]comp|dexa|fat[ _-]loss|weight[ _-](loss|gain)|precision nutrition|lyle mcdonald|energy availability|red-?s\b|ben house|renaissance periodization|caffeine",

COLLECTIONS = {
    "Mike Golden library": r"Golden, Mike",
    "Old Bull Performance": r"old ?bull",
    "Harries On-Field RTP (Sportsmith)": r"SS.Course.OnFieldRTP",
    "CVASPS": r"cvasp",
    "ALTIS": r"altis",
    "Charlie Francis": r"charlie ?francis",
}
COLLECTION_RULES = {k: re.compile(v, re.I) for k, v in COLLECTIONS.items()}

# Eric's own generated reports and dashboards: a record of practice, not literature.
OWN_REPORTS = re.compile(r"DASHBOARDS_AND_REPORTS|Report_Templates", re.I)


def route(row: dict) -> str:
    if OWN_REPORTS.search(row["path"]):
        return "Eric's reports (archive)"
    if row.get("in_zotero") == "True":
        return "already in Zotero"
    kind, size = row["kind"], int(row["size"] or 0)
    if kind in ("video", "audio"):
        return "transcription queue"
    if kind == "paper_or_book":
        if row["ext"] in ("epub", "mobi") or size >= 8_000_000:
            return "book (ingest-book, gated)"
        return "paper (Zotero)"
    if kind in ("document", "slides"):
        return "vault atomize"
    if kind == "data":
        return "template or data (review)"
    return "catalog only"


def main() -> None:
    with open(DATA / "manifest.csv", encoding="utf-8-sig") as fh:
        rows = [r for r in csv.DictReader(fh) if r["canonical"] == "True"]
    out, unclassified = [], []
    for r in rows:
        # A Zotero title (recovered by md5) rescues files named only by a Drive ID.
        text = f"{r['source']}/{r['path']} {r.get('zotero_title', '')}".replace("_", " ")
        rt = route(r)
        # Reports keep no discipline tags so they do not inflate the literature counts.
        tags = [] if rt == "Eric's reports (archive)" else [k for k, rx in RULES.items() if rx.search(text)]
        colls = [c for c in (r.get("collections") or "").split(";") if c]
        colls += [k for k, rx in COLLECTION_RULES.items() if rx.search(text)]
        r = {**r, "disciplines": ";".join(tags), "route": rt, "collections": ";".join(sorted(set(colls)))}
        out.append(r)
        if not tags and rt != "Eric's reports (archive)":
            unclassified.append(r)
    fields = list(out[0])
    for name, subset in (("triage.csv", out), ("unclassified.csv", unclassified)):
        with open(DATA / name, "w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            w = csv.DictWriter(fh, fieldnames=fields)
            w.writeheader()
            w.writerows(subset)

    disc = Counter(t for r in out for t in r["disciplines"].split(";") if t)
    routes = Counter(r["route"] for r in out)
    reports = sum(r["route"] == "Eric's reports (archive)" for r in out)
    lit = len(out) - reports
    lines = [
        "# Flint triage summary (rules pass)", "",
        f"Unique files: {len(out)}, of which {reports} are Eric's own reports and dashboards (archived, not classified). "
        f"Of the other {lit}, the rules classified {lit - len(unclassified)} ({100 * (lit - len(unclassified)) / lit:.0f}%); "
        f"{len(unclassified)} are left for the model pass (`data/unclassified.csv`).",
        "A file can carry several disciplines, so discipline counts sum to more than the file count.", "",
        "## By discipline", "", "| Discipline | Files | Papers/books | Video/audio |", "|---|---:|---:|---:|",
    ]
    for k, n in disc.most_common():
        sub = [r for r in out if k in r["disciplines"].split(";")]
        pb = sum(r["kind"] == "paper_or_book" for r in sub)
        av = sum(r["kind"] in ("video", "audio") for r in sub)
        lines.append(f"| {k} | {n} | {pb} | {av} |")
    lines += ["", "## By route", "", "| Route | Files |", "|---|---:|"]
    lines += [f"| {k} | {n} |" for k, n in routes.most_common()]
    coll = Counter(c for r in out for c in r["collections"].split(";") if c)
    lines += ["", "## Named collections", "", "| Collection | Files | Papers/books | Video/audio |", "|---|---:|---:|---:|"]
    for k, n in coll.most_common():
        sub = [r for r in out if k in r["collections"].split(";")]
        pb = sum(r["kind"] == "paper_or_book" for r in sub)
        av = sum(r["kind"] in ("video", "audio") for r in sub)
        lines.append(f"| {k} | {n} | {pb} | {av} |")
    (DATA / "triage_summary.md").write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
    print("\n".join(lines))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

201:## Named influences
# Flint

Flint is Claude working as Eric's sport-science, performance, S&C and rehab thought
partner. The name comes from Proverbs 27:17 ("iron sharpens iron"): the job is to
sharpen Eric's reasoning, not soothe it.

This repo holds the knowledge-ingest project that feeds Flint. It is a **side-lane**
project (outside the prioritization-slate cap, by Eric's choice on 2026-09-26). No
charter. It runs as small background batches during the season.

## The idea

Claude does not learn from files. What makes Flint better is what is stored and
findable: Zotero full text, SecondBrain vault notes, and above all **per-discipline
synthesis notes** that record where the sources agree, where they disagree, and
where Eric lands. So the job is not "ingest everything". It has three layers:

1. **Catalog everything** with a script, spending no tokens (step 0 below).
2. **Deep-ingest a short ranked list.**
3. **Synthesize one discipline at a time.** This layer is the thought partner.

## Steps

| Step | What | Tool | State |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | Manifest + dedup of all sources (metadata only, via the Drive API) | `scripts/build_manifest.ps1` | built 2026-09-26 |
| 1 | Eric's own method: Applied Performance Playbook, AP Assessment Manual V12, HHPR 5355 transcripts, force-plate protocols, Sportsmith articles, plus his written decision rules (via `/interview-me`) | Claude | next |
| 2 | Triage each unique file: discipline + tier (A deep-ingest / B catalog only / C skip) | Haiku + Codex | |
| 3 | Route tier A by type: papers → Zotero (after its 92-item queue clears); courses with transcripts → vault atomization; books → `ingest-book` behind the review gate; video → overnight transcription queue | existing pipelines | |
| 4 | Per-discipline synthesis notes (e.g. hamstring RTP: Harries vs Landon vs TB/David Grey vs Eric's manual) | Claude + Eric review | |

Eric's own material goes first for a structural reason. Every synthesis note compares
a source against how Eric already works, and that comparison is impossible until his
method is in.

## Sources

The roots are listed in `config/roots.json`. To add a source, edit the list; the code
does not change.

- Eric's Drive: 07_EDUCATION, 06_TEMPLATES, SPORT_SCIENCE, 09_PRO_DEV,
  From_REMOTE_DESK (this includes **Landon Evans**, about 800 files), 04_RESEARCH.
- My Drive, outside `00_Primary_Storage_Drive`: **Athletic Performance & Sports
  Science** (Literature & Textbooks, Training Programs & Planners, Coach Lowe's
  material, Seminars & Presentations with Pfaff, Moyer and Korfist), **RTP Clinic —
  Take-Home Resources**, and **Research Papers**. `Zotero_PDFs` is excluded because
  Zotero owns it, and `CATAPULT_HUB_PRO` is excluded because it is athlete data.
- **TB's Training Info**: Thomas Barbeau's shared folder. 2,179 files, 75 GB, about 80
  coaches or systems (SC Books, Stop Chasing Pain, DNS, David Grey Rehab, Burdenko,
  ALTIS, ELDOA, ...). It is **not synced locally** and is still being edited by its
  owner, so snapshot it with `gws` before ingesting.
- Shared folders: the Pro Football Sports Science Research Update issues, the 2026
  CSCCa conference presentations, the Enoka ISB talk, and coach Lowe's drill folders.

## Rules

- **DexaProject, athlete data, Catapult and PFF exports are never catalogued**
  (`exclude_path_regex`). Spreadsheets and images are kept (Eric lifted the privacy filter 2026-09-26).
- **Codex workers only ever see staged copies**, in a scratch folder, never the Drive
  root. Codex is an external service. Pilot one batch before fanning out.

1. Enrich. Files in 04_RESEARCH/_INBOX/drive-zotero-import_2026-06/pdfs-pass* are named
   by their original Drive id. The June import logs in that folder map each id to its
   original file name, folder, Crossref title and Zotero import status. First-page text
   from the logs' *-unresolved.txt files is used too.
2. Rules. The rules-pass disciplines plus extra keyword rules (EXTRA) run on the
   enriched text; skip rules (SKIP) mark admin, personal, photo and athlete-data files
   as tier C.
3. Model labels. Whatever is left was labelled by Claude from path, name and first-page
   text in batches: data/model_labels/*.csv (columns: key, disciplines, tier, route,
   reason). A model label always wins over a rule, so a rule mistake can be corrected
   by labelling the file.

Writes data/triage_model_pass.csv (gitignored) and data/triage_model_summary.md.
Tier: A deep-ingest candidate, B catalog only (paper to Zotero in bulk counts as B
unless it is on a shortlist), C skip.
"""

from collections import Counter
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent))
from triage_rules import RULES  # noqa: E402

DATA = ROOT / "data"
IMPORT = Path(os.environ.get(
    "FLINT_IMPORT_DIR",
    "G:/My Drive/00_Primary_Storage_Drive/04_RESEARCH/_INBOX/drive-zotero-import_2026-06"))

# Tier C on sight: admin, personal, photo dumps, system files, athlete data.
SKIP = [
    ("athlete data", r"dexa|athlete.?snapshot|catapult.?(export|hub)|\bpff\b|jump.?reports?|completed.?sheets|\b(sp|fa|su)\d\d.?dailys|team.?competition|testing.?results|roster|\bscores?\b.*\.xlsx?$|combine.?results"),
    ("admin or personal", r"receipt|invoice|payment|paystub|\btax|txtag|uber|itinerary|resume|\bcv\b|cover.?letter|coverletter|reference.?letter|recommendation.?letter|\bgmail\b|live assistance|online return|order.?confirm|boarding|reservation|w-?2|1099|lease|insurance|medical bill|bswhealth|\bvb sign up|sign.?up|schedule.?(fall|spring)|master schedule|expense|reimburs|budget|travel.?auth|parking|passport|headshot|business card|org.?chart|job.?(posting|description)|application|offer letter|contract|agenda|minutes|\bmemo\b"),
    ("system or empty", r"thumbs\.db$|desktop\.ini$|\.ds_store$|\.lnk$|~\$|\.tmp$|\.json$|\.db$|untitled|\bcopy of copy\b"),
    ("photo or raw video", r"\.(jpe?g|jfif|png|heic|gif|tif|bmp)$|\b(img|dsc|_i2p|vid|mvi|gopr)[_ ]?\d{3,}"),
]
SKIP_RULES = [(k, re.compile(v, re.I)) for k, v in SKIP]


def import_index() -> dict:
    """Map Drive id -> original name, folder, Crossref title, Zotero status, first page."""
    idx: dict = {}
    if not IMPORT.exists():
        print(f"warning: import folder not found: {IMPORT}", file=sys.stderr)
        return idx
    for f in sorted(IMPORT.glob("*.json")):
        try:
            d = json.loads(f.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        except Exception:
            continue
        items = d if isinstance(d, list) else (list(d.values()) if isinstance(d, dict) else [])
        for r in items:
            if not isinstance(r, dict):
                continue
            s = r["source"] if isinstance(r.get("source"), dict) else r
            if "id" not in s or "name" not in s:
                continue
            e = idx.setdefault(s["id"], {"name": s["name"], "folder": "", "title": "", "journal": "",
                                         "zotero": "", "first": "", "scholarly": ""})
            e["folder"] = e["folder"] or (s.get("folder_path") or "")
            cr = s.get("crossref") if isinstance(s.get("crossref"), dict) else None
            if cr and not e["title"]:
                t = cr.get("title")
                e["title"] = (t[0] if isinstance(t, list) and t else t or "") if t else ""
                j = cr.get("container-title")
                e["journal"] = (j[0] if isinstance(j, list) and j else j or "") if j else ""
            if str(s.get("scholarly")) in ("True", "False") and not e["scholarly"]:
                e["scholarly"] = str(s.get("scholarly"))
    for f in sorted(IMPORT.glob("*.ndjson")):
        for line in f.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
            try:
                s = json.loads(line)
            except Exception:
                continue
            if isinstance(s, dict) and "id" in s and "name" in s:
                idx.setdefault(s["id"], {"name": s["name"], "folder": s.get("folder_path", ""), "title": "",
                                         "journal": "", "zotero": "", "first": "", "scholarly": ""})
    st = IMPORT / "import-state.json"
    if st.exists():
        for v in json.loads(st.read_text(encoding="utf-8")).values():
            sid = v.get("source_id")
            if sid in idx:
                idx[sid]["zotero"] = v.get("status", "")
                idx[sid]["title"] = idx[sid]["title"] or v.get("title", "")
    for f in sorted(IMPORT.glob("*unresolved*.txt")):
        for block in re.split(r"^### ", f.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace"), flags=re.M):
            head, _, body = block.partition("\n")
            sid = head.split(" | ")[0].strip()
            if sid in idx and not idx[sid]["first"]:
                idx[sid]["first"] = " ".join(body.split())[:600]
    return idx


def load_labels() -> dict:
    labels = {}
    for f in sorted(glob.glob(str(DATA / "model_labels" / "*.csv"))):
        with open(f, encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            for r in csv.DictReader(fh):
                if r.get("key"):
                    labels[r["key"].strip()] = r
    return labels


def default_route(r: dict, discs: list) -> str:
    kind, ext, size = r["kind"], r["ext"], int(r["size"] or 0)
    if r.get("in_zotero") == "True" or r.get("zotero_status") in ("verified", "skipped_existing_pdf"):
        return "already in Zotero"
    if kind in ("video", "audio"):
        return "transcribe"
    if kind == "paper_or_book":
        if ext in ("epub", "mobi") or size >= 8_000_000:
            return "book"
        return "paper to Zotero"
    if kind in ("document", "slides"):
        return "atomize"
    return "catalog only"


def main() -> None:
    with open(DATA / "unclassified.csv", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        rows = list(csv.DictReader(fh))
    idx = import_index()
    labels = load_labels()
    out = []
    for r in rows:
        key = r["md5"] or r["id"]
        stem = r["name"].rsplit(".", 1)[0]
        e = idx.get(stem) if "drive-zotero-import" in r["path"] else None
        orig_name = e["name"] if e else ""
        orig_folder = e["folder"] if e else ""
        title = (e["title"] if e else "") or r.get("zotero_title", "")
        first = e["first"] if e else ""
        zstat = e["zotero"] if e else ""
        text = " ".join([r["source"], r["path"], orig_folder, orig_name, title]).replace("_", " ")
        rich = text + " " + first
        rr = {**r, "zotero_status": zstat}
        how, discs, tier, route, reason = "", [], "", "", ""
        lab = labels.get(key)
        skip = next((k for k, rx in SKIP_RULES if rx.search(text)), None)
        if lab:
            how = "model"
            discs = [d.strip() for d in (lab.get("disciplines") or "").split(";") if d.strip()]
            tier, route, reason = lab.get("tier", ""), lab.get("route", ""), lab.get("reason", "")
        elif skip:
            how, tier, route, reason = "rule", "C", "skip", f"skip rule: {skip}"
        else:
            discs = [k for k, rx in RULES.items() if rx.search(rich)]
            discs += [k for k, rx in EXTRA_RULES.items() if rx.search(rich) and k not in discs]
            if discs:
                how, tier = "rule", "B"
                route = default_route(rr, discs)
                reason = "keyword rules on " + ("original name, folder and first page" if e else "path and name")
        if how and route != "skip" and zstat in ("verified", "skipped_existing_pdf"):
            route = "already in Zotero"
        out.append({
            "key": key, "source": r["source"], "path": r["path"], "name": r["name"], "ext": r["ext"],
            "kind": r["kind"], "size": r["size"], "orig_name": orig_name, "orig_folder": orig_folder,
            "title": title, "first_page": first[:300], "zotero_status": zstat, "collections": r["collections"],
            "disciplines": ";".join(discs), "tier": tier, "route": route, "reason": reason, "how": how,
        })
    fields = list(out[0])
    with open(DATA / "triage_model_pass.csv", "w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        w = csv.DictWriter(fh, fieldnames=fields)
        w.writeheader()
        w.writerows(out)
    todo = [o for o in out if not o["how"]]
    with open(DATA / "model_todo.csv", "w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        w = csv.DictWriter(fh, fieldnames=fields)
        w.writeheader()
        w.writerows(todo)
    print("rows", len(out), "how", Counter(o["how"] or "todo" for o in out))
    print("tier", Counter(o["tier"] for o in out), "route", Counter(o["route"] for o in out))
    write_summary(out)


def write_summary(out: list) -> None:
    n = len(out)
    how = Counter(o["how"] or "unlabelled" for o in out)
    tiers = Counter(o["tier"] or "unlabelled" for o in out)
    routes = Counter(o["route"] or "unlabelled" for o in out)
    disc = Counter(d for o in out for d in o["disciplines"].split(";") if d)
    lines = [
        "# Flint triage summary (model pass)", "",
        f"Files the keyword rules left unclassified: {n} (`data/unclassified.csv`). "
        "This pass enriched the 1,310 Drive-id-named PDFs from the June Zotero import logs, "
        "ran extra keyword and skip rules, then Claude labelled the rest in batches from path, "
        "name and first-page text (`data/model_labels/`). Script: `scripts/triage_model_pass.py`. "
        "File-level output: `data/triage_model_pass.csv` (gitignored).", "",
        "## How each file was labelled", "", "| Method | Files |", "|---|---:|",
    ]
    lines += [f"| {k} | {v} |" for k, v in how.most_common()]
    lines += ["", "## By tier", "", "| Tier | Files |", "|---|---:|"]
    names = {"A": "A deep-ingest candidate", "B": "B catalog only", "C": "C skip"}
    lines += [f"| {names.get(k, k)} | {v} |" for k, v in sorted(tiers.items())]
    lines += ["", "## By route", "", "| Route | Files | Tier A |", "|---|---:|---:|"]
    lines += [f"| {k} | {v} | {sum(1 for o in out if o['route'] == k and o['tier'] == 'A')} |"
              for k, v in routes.most_common()]
    lines += ["", "## By discipline (tiers A and B)", "",
              "A file can carry several disciplines.", "", "| Discipline | Files | Tier A |", "|---|---:|---:|"]
    for k, _ in disc.most_common():
        sub = [o for o in out if k in o["disciplines"].split(";") and o["tier"] in ("A", "B")]
        lines.append(f"| {k} | {len(sub)} | {sum(o['tier'] == 'A' for o in sub)} |")
    skips = Counter(o["reason"] for o in out if o["tier"] == "C")
    lines += ["", "## Tier C reasons (top 15)", "", "| Reason | Files |", "|---|---:|"]
    lines += [f"| {k} | {v} |" for k, v in skips.most_common(15)]
    (DATA / "triage_model_summary.md").write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

163	        stem = r["name"].rsplit(".", 1)[0]

165	        orig_name = e["name"] if e else ""
166	        orig_folder = e["folder"] if e else ""

168	        first = e["first"] if e else ""
169	        zstat = e["zotero"] if e else ""

171	        rich = text + " " + first

178	                         orig_name or r["name"]]).replace("_", " ")
179	        near_ = " ".join([r["path"].rsplit("/", 2)[-2] if r["path"].count("/") >= 1 else "", orig_name or r["name"]])
180	        skip = next((k for k, rx in SKIP_RULES if rx.search(near) or rx.search(near_)), None)
181	        if lab:
182	            how = "model"
183	            discs = [d.strip() for d in (lab.get("disciplines") or "").split(";") if d.strip()]
184	            tier, route, reason = lab.get("tier", ""), lab.get("route", ""), lab.get("reason", "")
185	        elif skip:

187	        else:
188	            # Rules read the name, folders and Crossref title, not the first page: first
189	            # pages carry affiliations and abstracts that trip half the keywords.
190	            discs = [k for k, rx in RULES.items() if rx.search(text)]
191	            discs += [k for k, rx in EXTRA_RULES.items() if rx.search(text) and k not in discs]
192	            # More than three hits means the keywords are guessing; send it to the model.
193	            if 0 < len(discs) <= 3:
194	                how, tier = "rule", "B"
195	                route = default_route(rr, discs)
196	                reason = "keyword rules on " + ("original name, folder and first page" if e else "path and name")
197	        if how and route != "skip" and zstat in ("verified", "skipped_existing_pdf"):
198	            route = "already in Zotero"

201	            "kind": r["kind"], "size": r["size"], "orig_name": orig_name, "orig_folder": orig_folder,
202	            "title": title, "first_page": first[:300], "zotero_status": zstat, "collections": r["collections"],
203	            "disciplines": ";".join(discs), "tier": tier, "route": route, "reason": reason, "how": how,
204	        })

206	    with open(DATA / "triage_model_pass.csv", "w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
207	        w = csv.DictWriter(fh, fieldnames=fields)
208	        w.writeheader()
209	        w.writerows(out)
210	    todo = [o for o in out if not o["how"]]
211	    with open(DATA / "model_todo.csv", "w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
212	        w = csv.DictWriter(fh, fieldnames=fields)
213	        w.writeheader()
214	        w.writerows(todo)
215	    print("rows", len(out), "how", Counter(o["how"] or "todo" for o in out))

entries.name: Monitor
entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

When an event lands that the user would want to act on now — an error appeared, the status they were waiting on flipped — send a PushNotification. Not every event is worth a push; the ones that change what they'd do next are.

description.description: Short human-readable description of what you are monitoring (shown in notifications).

timeout_ms.description: Kill the monitor after this deadline. Default 300000ms. Deadlines above 1800000ms are capped to 1800000ms. You are notified at expiry and can re-arm.

command.description: Shell command or script. Each stdout line is an event; exit ends the watch.

ws.description: WebSocket to open. Each text frame is an event; binary frames are reported as a placeholder line. Socket close ends the watch. Cannot be combined with command.

entries.name: TaskStop
entries.description:
- Stops a running background task by its ID
- Takes a task_id parameter identifying the task to stop
- To stop an agent-team teammate, pass its agent ID ("name@team") or bare teammate name as task_id
- To stop a background agent spawned with a name, pass that name as task_id
- Returns a success or failure status
- Use this tool when you need to terminate a long-running task

task_id.description: The ID of the background task to stop. Agent-team teammates and named background agents are also accepted by agent ID or name.

"""Build per-discipline candidate pools for the shortlist agents (scratch, not committed)."""
import csv
import sys
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "scripts"))
from triage_model_pass import import_index  # noqa: E402

DATA = ROOT / "data"
idx = import_index()
SLUGS = {
    "Rehab and return to play": "rehab-and-return-to-play",
    "Speed and sprint": "speed-and-sprint",
    "Strength and power": "strength-and-power",
    "Conditioning and energy systems": "conditioning-and-energy-systems",
    "Load monitoring and GPS": "load-monitoring",
    "Recovery and sleep": "recovery-and-sleep",
    "Nutrition and body composition": "nutrition",
    "Periodization and programming": "periodization-and-programming",
    "Testing and assessment": "testing-and-assessment",
}
rows = []
with open(DATA / "triage.csv", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
    for r in csv.DictReader(fh):
        if not r["disciplines"] or r["route"] == "Eric's reports (archive)" or r["kind"] in ("image", "archive"):
            continue
        e = idx.get(r["id"]) or idx.get("md5:" + r["md5"])
        rows.append({"key": r["md5"] or r["id"], "source": r["source"], "path": r["path"], "kind": r["kind"],
                     "ext": r["ext"], "size_mb": round(int(r["size"] or 0) / 1e6, 1),
                     "pages": (e or {}).get("pages", ""), "collections": r["collections"], "route": r["route"],
                     "in_zotero": r["in_zotero"], "title": r["zotero_title"] or (e or {}).get("title", ""),
                     "dup_count": r["dup_count"], "reason": "rules pass", "disciplines": r["disciplines"]})
with open(DATA / "triage_model_pass.csv", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
    for r in csv.DictReader(fh):
        if r["tier"] not in ("A", "B") or "own material" in r["route"] or r["kind"] in ("image", "archive"):
            continue
        path = r["path"] if not r["orig_name"] else f"{r['path']} (originally {r['orig_folder']}/{r['orig_name']})"
        rows.append({"key": r["key"], "source": r["source"], "path": path, "kind": r["kind"], "ext": r["ext"],
                     "size_mb": round(int(r["size"] or 0) / 1e6, 1), "pages": r["pages"],
                     "collections": r["collections"], "route": r["route"],
                     "in_zotero": "True" if r["route"] == "already in Zotero" else "False", "title": r["title"],
                     "dup_count": "", "reason": ("candidate: " if r.get("candidate") == "yes" else "") + r["reason"],
                     "disciplines": r["disciplines"]})
out = DATA / "_tmp" / "pools"
out.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
cols = ["key", "source", "path", "kind", "ext", "size_mb", "pages", "collections", "route", "in_zotero",
        "title", "dup_count", "reason"]
for d, slug in SLUGS.items():
    sub = [r for r in rows if d in r["disciplines"].split(";")]
    with open(out / f"{slug}.csv", "w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        w = csv.DictWriter(fh, fieldnames=cols, extrasaction="ignore")
        w.writeheader()
        w.writerows(sub)
    print(slug, len(sub))
